site.name: notion
site.summary: notion-clone Clone of the Notion marketing funnel: home + product sub-pages + templates + pricing. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Home: top nav (Product / Download / Solutions / Resources / Pricing / Request demo / Log in / Get Notion free), hero section (product positioning + CTA + main screenshot), modular product intros (Docs / Wikis / Projects / AI), customer logo wall, customer stories, multi-column footer | | `projects.html` | Project management sub-page: feature highlights, view-switching screenshots (Board / Timeline / Calendar), case studies, CTA | | `wikis.html` | Wiki sub-page: knowledge-base examples, permissions / search / template features, CTA |

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full notion system, prioritizing the primary landing flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The Notion clone site suffers from critical interaction failures that severely degrade the user experience, most notably non-functional FAQ accordions across all pages and a complete lack of form validation or submission feedback. Mobile usability is compromised by pervasive small tap targets, a broken hamburger menu, and horizontal overflow on the pricing page. While navigation between pages and modal triggers generally function, the dead-end interactions and missing feedback create significant friction for users attempting to complete conversion goals.

exploration_plan.goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full Notion marketing clone, validating the primary landing flow, product sub-pages, pricing interactions, and mobile responsiveness.
exploration_plan.summary: The exploration will start by validating the primary conversion flow on the home page, including CTAs and modals. It will then systematically traverse the product sub-pages (Projects, Wikis) and Templates to verify content rendering and cross-linking. Next, it will deep-dive into the Pricing page's interactive elements like toggles and accordions. Finally, the entire critical flow will be re-evaluated on a mobile viewport to assess layout warnings and tap target usability.
assumptions: CTAs like 'Request a demo' and 'Get Notion free' trigger JavaScript modals or dialogs rather than navigating to new pages.
The pricing toggle switches between Monthly and Yearly views dynamically without a page reload.
FAQ accordions on Pricing and Templates pages expand and collapse content interactively.
The site is a static frontend clone with no backend, so form submissions will not result in actual data saves.
risk_hotspots: Small tap targets on navigation links and footer links, especially problematic on mobile viewports.
Pricing toggle (Monthly/Yearly) state changes and ensuring price values update correctly.
Modal dialogs triggered by 'Request a demo' and 'Get Notion free' might lack proper close mechanisms or focus trapping.
FAQ accordion buttons might not provide clear visual feedback when expanded/collapsed.

phases.title: Home Page & Primary Flow
phases.objective: Validate the main landing page structure, primary conversion CTAs, and modal interactions.
key_checks: Verify hero section layout and content visibility.
Click 'Request a demo' and validate the resulting dialog/modal content and close behavior.
Click 'Get Notion free' and validate the resulting dialog/modal content and close behavior.
Scroll through modular product intros and verify section transitions.
exit_criteria: Both primary CTAs have been clicked and their modals successfully closed.
Full page scroll from top to footer completed without layout shifts.

phases.title: Product Sub-pages Exploration
phases.objective: Navigate through Projects and Wikis pages to validate content rendering, feature sections, and cross-navigation.
key_checks: Navigate to Projects page via top nav and verify feature highlights load correctly.
Check cross-linking CTAs on Projects page (e.g., 'Wikis Centralize all your knowledge...').
Navigate to Wikis page via top nav and verify knowledge-base examples render.
Check cross-linking CTAs on Wikis page (e.g., 'Projects Manage any type of project...').
exit_criteria: Both Projects and Wikis pages have been visited from the top nav.
At least one cross-link CTA on each page has been clicked and verified.

phases.title: Templates & Pricing Interactions
phases.objective: Deep-dive into interactive elements on the Templates and Pricing pages, specifically toggles and accordions.
key_checks: Navigate to Templates page and click at least two FAQ accordion buttons to verify expand/collapse behavior.
Navigate to Pricing page and interact with the 'Toggle yearly pricing' control, verifying that prices update.
Click FAQ buttons on Pricing page (e.g., 'How does Notion AI use my data?') to check content expansion.
Verify 'Sign up', 'Get started', and 'Contact Sales' buttons presence and click behavior.
exit_criteria: Pricing toggle has been switched back and forth at least once.
At least one FAQ accordion on Templates and one on Pricing have been expanded.
CTA buttons on Pricing have been interacted with.

phases.title: Mobile Viewport Validation
phases.objective: Re-evaluate the critical flows and layout warnings on a mobile viewport to ensure responsive design integrity.
key_checks: Switch to mobile viewport and verify Home page hero section stacks correctly.
Validate tap target spacing for top navigation links on mobile.
Check Pricing page toggle and accordions usability on mobile.
Verify modals ('Request a demo') are usable and do not overflow screen boundaries on mobile.
exit_criteria: Home and Pricing pages viewed on mobile without horizontal overflow.
Mobile tap target warnings visually validated for top nav.
Modal interactions successfully completed on mobile viewport.

coverage_targets.features: exercise all visible modals, pricing toggles, and at least one FAQ accordion per relevant page
coverage_targets.mobile: repeat critical checks (Home CTAs, Pricing toggle) on mobile viewport

notes: Pay close attention to the small_tap_target layout warnings identified in the prescan, particularly when switching to the mobile viewport in Phase 4.
Since this is a clone, verify that 'javascript:void(0)' links correctly trigger expected UI components like modals instead of failing silently.

findings.user_goal: Get answers to pricing and product questions
findings.problem: FAQ accordion buttons across the Pricing and Templates pages do not expand or reveal answers when clicked, providing zero visual feedback.
findings.evidence: Clicking FAQ buttons like 'How does Notion AI use my data?', 'What are your accepted payment methods?', 'Do you offer student discounts?', and 'What project management templates should I start with?' resulted in 'No obvious URL or visible-text change' (steps-07-12, steps-25-30, steps-55-60, steps-43-48).
findings.why_it_matters: Users rely on FAQs to resolve purchase hesitations and understand product details. Broken accordions leave users stranded without answers, directly impacting trust and conversion.
findings.suggestion: Implement functional expand/collapse JavaScript for the FAQ sections and ensure ARIA expanded states are toggled for accessibility.

findings.user_goal: Sign up or request a demo
findings.problem: Submitting forms with empty required fields (Work email, Full name, Company name) triggers no validation errors, success messages, or loading states.
findings.evidence: Clicking 'Continue' or 'Submit request' with blank required fields resulted in no visible change or feedback (steps-13-18, steps-61-66).
findings.why_it_matters: Users are left guessing whether their submission went through or failed, leading to frustration, repeated clicks, and potential abandonment of the conversion flow.
findings.suggestion: Add client-side validation to highlight missing required fields with clear error messages, and provide a success state or loading indicator upon valid submission.
findings.source_hint: index.html, pricing.html (Sign up / Request a demo modals)

findings.user_goal: Navigate the site on a mobile device
findings.problem: The mobile hamburger menu toggle fails to open the navigation overlay on the pricing page.
findings.evidence: Clicking the 'Toggle menu' button (ux-2) on the mobile viewport of pricing.html resulted in 'No obvious URL or visible-text change' (step agentic-77-click).
findings.why_it_matters: Mobile users are completely blocked from accessing primary navigation, effectively trapping them on the pricing page unless they use footer links.
findings.suggestion: Debug the mobile menu toggle JavaScript to ensure the navigation overlay opens and closes reliably across all pages.

findings.user_goal: Interact with the site on a mobile device
findings.problem: Critical interactive elements, including the modal close button, hamburger menu, and footer links, have tap targets well below the 44px minimum mobile guidance.
findings.evidence: The modal close button is 14x24px, the hamburger menu is 36x32px, and footer links are 342x22px. Layout warnings repeatedly flagged these across mobile viewports (steps-67-72, steps-73-78, agentic-80-click).
findings.why_it_matters: Undersized tap targets cause accidental mis-taps and make the interface frustrating and difficult to use for touch users, particularly for essential actions like closing a modal.
findings.suggestion: Increase the padding and hit areas for the close button, hamburger menu, and footer links to meet the 44x44px minimum touch target size.

findings.user_goal: Browse the pricing page on mobile
findings.problem: The pricing page has a horizontal overflow on mobile, causing the page width to exceed the viewport width.
findings.evidence: A medium severity horizontal overflow was detected on the mobile viewport: page width is 399px, exceeding the 390px viewport width (steps-73-78).
findings.why_it_matters: Horizontal overflow forces users to swipe sideways, breaking the expected vertical scroll flow and making the page feel broken or poorly designed.
findings.suggestion: Audit the CSS on the pricing page to ensure all containers and elements are constrained to 100% viewport width using responsive units and overflow-hidden where appropriate.

findings.problem: Several primary CTAs use 'javascript:void(0)' hrefs, and while some correctly trigger modals, others (like 'Sign up' on pricing) are dead links with no feedback.
findings.evidence: Clicking 'Sign up' on the pricing page resulted in no visible change or navigation, confirming it as a dead link (steps-07-12). Other links like 'Get Notion free' successfully opened modals despite using the same href pattern.
findings.why_it_matters: Inconsistent CTA behavior erodes user trust. When a primary action like 'Sign up' does nothing, users may assume the site is broken and leave.
findings.suggestion: Ensure all CTAs have functional event handlers. Replace 'javascript:void(0)' with proper button elements or ensure the JS handlers are consistently attached and accessible.

findings.problem: Clicking the 'Knowledge Base' footer link on the wikis.html page does nothing because it links to the current page, providing no feedback.
findings.evidence: Clicking 'Knowledge Base' on wikis.html resulted in no visible change or URL update, as the link points to the current page (steps-31-36).
findings.why_it_matters: Users may think the click failed or the site is unresponsive, leading to confusion.
findings.suggestion: Visually distinguish the active page link in the footer (e.g., bold or different color) or remove the link for the current page to prevent dead-end clicks.
